experiment: single post-picker normalized positive spectral-change gate

parameters.formula: accept native peak i iff D_i > 0 and native_flux_i / D_i >= 0.5, where D_i = max over j in clipped [i-8,i+8] of sum of one-sided magnitude bins in actual PCM support j
parameters.numeric_contract: native FFT magnitudes and flux are f32; spectrum mass and quotient use f64 accumulation; no epsilon or PCM-volume cutoff
parameters.short_file_and_tail: unchanged real support windows from frozen spectral probe; no padding
parameters.coordinate: unchanged native candidate's integer center of actual PCM support
parameters.threshold_rationale: require new positive spectral magnitude at least half the largest nearby total spectral magnitude; use the native picker's existing context to avoid an adjacent phase minimum as denominator; this fixed research criterion is not perceptually calibrated

inputs.cases: all existing 18 strict cases, all 6 new discrete controls, and the continuous fade observation from the frozen report
inputs.pcm: reuse original landed f32le inputs without regeneration or alteration
inputs.labels: use the frozen report's independently declared labels only after analysis, with the original matcher and unchanged all-match/zero-extra/median<=96-frame gate
inputs.continuous_fade: truth and metrics remain null; report peaks without scoring

required_invariants: Rerun the unmodified native Flux analyzer and compare every recorded native f32 strength bit, peak flag, support coordinate and prediction against the frozen report
Accepted predictions must be an ordered subset of unmodified native predictions at identical PCM coordinates
No output translation, frame-zero supplementation, new peak generation, truth-dependent parameters, threshold sweep or per-case tuning
Preserve all original FAIL cases and record newly introduced false negatives
declared_failure_boundaries: Native first-frame zero and unknown pre-file history remain unchanged
A weak onset close to a stronger event can be suppressed by the contextual denominator
Gradual attacks, continuous pitch changes and low-contrast overlapping notes may not change half the local spectral mass within one hop
Finite-window phase interference in low frequencies can still exceed the fixed criterion
A gain-invariant criterion cannot distinguish every noise fluctuation from an independently intended musical event
Real music, human annotation, confidence calibration, canonical Ogg readback and production MIR integration are outside this experiment
